entities.name: Polycrates of Ephesus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Polycrates of Ephesus was a pivotal figure in the Early Christian era, serving as bishop of Ephesus from approximately 155 to 196 CE. He convened the Synod of Ephesus, a gathering that established Quartodecimanism as the official position on Easter for Asia Minor.

This event had significant consequences, including the widespread adoption of Quartodeciman practices throughout the Eastern Roman Empire. The Synod's composition, dated to between 186 and 195 CE, provides valuable insights into the theological debates of the time.

Polycrates' legacy extends beyond his own era, as his synod's influence can be seen in the development of Christian liturgical practices and the ongoing debate over the date of Easter.

"The Lord is near to the broken-hearted and saves the oppressed." - Polycrates of Ephesus, Letter to the Roman Patriarch
